QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_28

question.text: Swasth Bharat Trust's immunisation program in a district achieves 90% coverage. State-wide trend data (without the Trust) shows 72% coverage in comparable districts. What is the deadweight percentage?

explanation.text: The Logic: In SROI / impact-evaluation practice, "deadweight" denotes the share of the observed outcome that would have occurred even in the absence of the intervention - typically estimated from a counterfactual (e.g., comparable districts without the programme). When expressed as a proportion of the gross outcome, deadweight = counterfactual outcome / gross outcome. Here, counterfactual coverage = 72% and gross outcome = 90%, so deadweight = 72 / 90 = 0.80 = 80%. That is, 80% of the observed coverage would have happened anyway via the state-wide trend; only the remaining 20% (the 18 percentage-point lift) is attributable to the Trust's programme. The Trap: 90% is the gross outcome itself, not the deadweight proportion. 72% is the absolute counterfactual coverage level, not deadweight as a proportion of the gross. 18% is the additional percentage points of coverage attributable to the programme (the absolute lift), not the deadweight proportion. The proportion answer is 72/90 = 80%. Note: The cited workbook pages (134, 146, 160 of the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook) support baseline / counterfactual and contribution concepts and list immunisation coverage as a health indicator, but they do not define "deadweight" or give the formula deadweight = counterfactual / gross outcome. The framing above reflects general SROI / impact-measurement practice as widely used in the field.
